{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study evaluates the utility of a 'core battery' of safety pharmacology studies in predicting clinical outcomes, specifically assessing the concordance between animal model findings and human clinical safety. It quantifies the utility and impact of these studies, aligning with the review's focus on animal model concordance with human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "Core battery safety pharmacology testing – An assessment of its utility in early drug development",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular",
    "neurology-stroke",
    "respiratory",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study explicitly mentions cardiovascular, central nervous system (CNS), and respiratory function studies as part of the core battery, and also lists a variety of therapeutic areas for the investigational drugs, including cardiovascular disease, neurology, and pneumology.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study evaluates multiple types of safety pharmacology studies including in vitro hERG assays, conscious non-rodent telemetry cardiovascular studies, rodent CNS (modified Irwin’s or functional observational battery [FOB] test) studies, and respiratory function (plethysmography) studies.",
  "species": [
    "rat",
    "dog",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study mentions the use of non-rodent telemetry cardiovascular studies, typically in Beagle dog or cynomolgus monkey, and rodent CNS and respiratory function studies, mainly in rats.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study discusses findings related to QTc interval, blood pressure, heart rate (secondary biomarkers), and also touches upon the utility of these studies in impacting clinical starting dose and safety/risk assessment (primary hard outcomes)."
}
